Hypoxia causes induction of hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF), which stimulates erythropoietin (EPO) synthesis. Prolyl hydroxylase domain (PHD) enzyme inhibition can stabilize hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF). HIF stabilization also decreases hepcidin, a hormone of hepatic origin, which regulates iron homeostasis. PHD inhibitors represent a novel pharmacological treatment of anemia associated with chronic diseases. This review discusses the role of PHD inhibitors in the treatment of anemia associated with chronic diseases.
